newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT - PepsiCo Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - PepsiCo Q1 earnings.

text.p: PepsiCo Tuesday morning announced first quarter earnings of $0.27 a share vs $0.24 a share in the same period a year earlier, beating First Call analysts' estimates of $0.24 a share for the first quarter.

The soft drink maker said first quarter sales rose to $6.7 billion from $6.55 billion and released more details of its plans to divest its restaurant businesses, including an IPO of New Zealand restarurants and its plan to sell California Pizza.
The following is the full text of the company's press release:

PURCHASE, N.Y., April 29 -- PepsiCo, Inc today announced results for the first quarter ended March 22, 1997. Sales grew two percent to $6.7 billion. Reported net income for the quarter grew eight percent to $427 million on top of 23% growth in the prior year. Earnings per share for the quarter were $0.27.

Roger Enrico, Chairman and CEO, stated: "We're pleased with our progress against our 1997 goals. Earnings and free cash flow are basically on track and we have stepped up the pace of our share repurchase program. To date, we've repurchased 20.7 million shares equal to 1.3 percent of the total shares outstanding at the start of the year.

"We are also on track with our restaurant strategy. We refranchised 94 stores this quarter and for the full year expect to sell as many or more than we did last year. We have made solid progress preparing for the planned spin-off of our quick service restaurant business including the preparation and filing of our ruling request with the IRS. In addition, we've

completed the sale of both East Side Mario's and Hot 'n Now. We have an agreement for the sale of Chevys and are in active discussions for the sale of both California Pizza Kitchen and PFS, our restaurant distribution company. Finally we are targeting the early summer for the initial public offering of our New Zealand restaurants.
"Although a lot has been accomplished, there is still a lot to do. However, I believe PepsiCo is becoming a far more focused company, and I am very excited about the year ahead."
Beverages

The most notable feature of our performance at Pepsi-Cola North America this quarter was solid volume growth on top of a strong performance in the first quarter of 1996. Bottler case sales grew six percent driven by a return to double-digit volume growth for Mountain Dew and solid growth in brand Pepsi. The growth was largely driven by favorable pricing in the take-home channels as lower packaging costs were passed through to the consumer. As a result of this combination of strong volume and lower pricing, sales advanced four percent. Operating profit grew three percent despite the difficult comparison to last year's 18 percent profit increase. Operating margins were basically unchanged despite the competitive environment.

International beverages (PCCI) volume was down three percent for the quarter. Although the change is still negative, it reflects an improvement over the nine percent volume decline reported in the fourth quarter. This improvement reflects our relaunch in Venezuela as well as better results across most regions despite the fact that the competition remains aggressive. As a result of lower bottler case sales, lower concentrate shipments and foreign exchange, sales were down 14 percent. As expected, PCCI posted a loss for the quarter which was largely the result of lower volume.
Snack Foods

Frito-Lay North America reported seven percent sales growth and 15 percent profit growth for the quarter. Sales growth was largely driven by four percent pound volume and higher pricing. The margin improvement also reflects flat advertising and marketing spending as well as favorable raw material costs.

Frito-Lay International sales and operating profit for the first quarter grew 13 percent and 36 percent, respectively. Sales growth was largely due to increases in effective net pricing and strong advances in volume. The volume contribution came from salty kilo growth of ten percent. Operating profits were favorably impacted by the gain on the sale of our interest in the Gerber business in Mexico. Otherwise, the business saw slight margin contraction primarily due to higher wheat costs.
Restaurants
Worldwide restaurant profits advanced seven percent as a result of strong results in the international business and a better than expected but modest increase in the U.S.

Looking at the operating results without the impact of net refranchising gains and the first quarter 1996 disposal charge for Hot 'n Now, the U.S. business had operating profit growth of six percent on a sales decline of two percent. The sales decline was driven by the fact that we had almost 800 fewer company-owned units in the first quarter of 1997 than we did in the first quarter of 1996 due to refranchising and store closures. Combined same store sales were not a factor in the total U.S. sales decline as the positive results at KFC and Taco Bell offset the decline, which had been anticipated, at Pizza Hut. Pizza Hut, the largest brand, had a same store

sales decline of eight percent due to the difficult comparison versus a year ago when Triple Decker pizza was launched. KFC and Taco Bell, however, both had positive same store sales growth of four percent in the quarter. In Taco Bell's case, the key driver was the success of the Star Wars promotion. At KFC, it was the continuation of strong trends in the core product portfolio. In fact, this quarter marks KFC's ninth consecutive quarter of same store sales growth. Favorable
trends in product mix and higher prices were key factors in operating profit growth for domestic restaurants.

International operating profit grew 22 percent on a three percent sales advance, which was moderated by an adjustment to conform Canada and Korea to international restaurant reporting periods. The sales increase was driven equally by new units and pricing. The one percentage point improvement in operating margins reflects the increase in fees and royalties from our franchise business. This income is expected to impact margins favorably going forward.
